item.title: The SDGs need a subjective well-being reality check
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01963-z

The Sustainable Development Goals aim to improve lives, but it is unclear whether progress on Sustainable Development Goal indicators translates into greater subjective well-being over time. A study of 42 countries found associations in levels, but weak links with year-to-year changes in life evaluations.
item.dc:title: The SDGs need a subjective well-being reality check
item.dc:creator: Mel George
Camille Wejnert-Depue
Anand Patwardhan

item.title: On living and feeling better
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01983-9

As the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) enter their final years, there is a desire to reflect on their societal impact. A study now compares changes in the SDG indicators with changes in how people feel about their lives and finds no detectable correlation between the two.
item.dc:title: On living and feeling better
item.dc:creator: Alberto Prati
Caspar Kaiser

item.title: Global socio-economic resilience to disasters
item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 29 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01947-z

Disaster risk assessments often overlook how damages affect well-being and recovery across populations. A global analysis now shows that well-being losses from disasters are much higher than asset damages, with the poorest suffering disproportionately.
item.dc:title: Global socio-economic resilience to disasters
item.dc:creator: Robin Middelanis
Bramka Arga Jafino
Ruth Hill
Minh Cong Nguyen
Stéphane Hallegatte
